resources.title: Start New Club
resources.description:
Start a Club
 
 Step-by-Step Process
 You may have many reasons for wanting to start a Toastmasters Club.
 For example, if you're interested in forming a Corporate Club, it might be because you'd like to give yourself and your colleagues the opportunity to build your communication and leadership skills together. If you're interested in forming a Community Club, it might be because you want to help yourself and others develop self-confidence and leadership potential.
 
 One of the most important things to consider before you start a Club is the Toastmasters club mission:
 "Toastmasters International provides a supportive and positive learning experience in which members are empowered to develop communication and leadership skills, resulting in greater self-confidence and personal growth."
 
 The Club you form should embody this mission. Starting a Toastmasters Club is an important responsibility and undertaking. It's your job to ensure that all members feel supported and that you have the resources to sustain and grow your membership. Providing a quality Club experience should be your primary goal.
 
 How to Start:
 STEP 1: Learn how Toastmasters works
 STEP 2: Decide what kind of Club you want to form
 STEP 3: Request a Club Sponsor
 STEP 4: Generate interest
 STEP 5: Charter your Club and set up a bank account
 STEP 6: Celebrate!
 
 Club Creation Forms
 Form 1 Application to Organize a Toastmasters Club – Form
 Form 2 Charter Payments – Form
 Form 3 Charter Membership Application (Individual) – Form
 Form 3 Charter Membership Application (Collective) – Excel Form
 Form 4 Charter Club Officer Information – Form
 Form 5 Club Information – Form
 Form 6A Club Constitution for Clubs of Toastmasters International – Form
 Form 6B Addendum of Standard Club Options – Form
 
 New Club Fee: $125 USD (one-time fee for the Club Startup Kit).
 New Member Fee: $25 USD per member (one-time fee for new Toastmasters members)
 Membership Dues: $60 USD per member (covers 6 months of membership)
 Chartering Requirement:
 • At least 20 members are required to charter a Club.
 • A Club with fewer than 20 members may be considered as a prospective Club (to be discussed).
 
 Stay tuned for an upcoming webinar on this topic

resources.description:
District Officers Roles
 
 From the Club to the Core Team: Leadership roles in Toastmasters
 Toastmasters is the best and most wonderful playground to experiment Leadership. Toastmasters do so all along their path, according to their willing to get responsibilities inside the organization.
 But… how is organized Leadership in Toastmasters? What are the roles you can fulfill if you want do do more for Toastmasters and your fellow members?
 Here are a few keys. Share them with all those you feel it could be useful to!
 
 What are the Leadership roles in the Club?
 The Club Officers consist of:
 President
 Vice-president Education | Vice-president Membership | Vice-president Public Relations
 Secretary | Treasurer | Sergeant-at-Arms
 Immediate Past President
 
 Are you a new officer in your Club, or a new President willing to help your team succeed?
 Find all the information you will need to reach your goals in the Club Leadership Handbook: in English | en Français | auf Deutsch
 …and find the very large range of tools Toastmasters makes available to help you with your mission: to provide a supportive and positive learning experience in which members are empowered to develop communication and leadership skills, resulting in greater self-confidence and personal growth. —–> here!
 
 What about the Leadership roles at the District level?
 The District Officers are the:
 The Core Team
 District Director | Program Quality Director | Club Growth Director (the trio) Public Relations Manager | Administration Manager | Finance Manager
 The District Officers
 Division Directors, Area Directors
 
 Meet the current District Team on their specific page, just > here < and complete your knowledge of how the District works with a precious resource: the District Leadership Handbook:

resources.description:
Club Officer Roles
 
 Toastmasters Clubs rely on a team of at least seven officers (board members) responsible for the smooth operation and success of the Club. Below is a summary of the roles and missions of each officer:
 [Infographics: Club President, Vice President Education, Vice President Membership, VPPR, Secretary, Treasurer, Sergeant at Arms]
 
 Each officer plays a crucial role in maintaining the quality and efficiency of meetings, thereby contributing to the development of members' communication and leadership skills.
 
 Want to develop your leadership further?
 Join the District Team!
 Toastmasters is an incredible platform to develop and practice leadership skills.
 Members have countless opportunities to step into leadership roles, guided by their desire to take on more responsibilities within the organization.
 But how exactly is leadership structured in Toastmasters?
 What roles can you explore if you're ready to contribute even more to Toastmasters and support your fellow members?
 Joining the District team is a fantastic way to elevate your leadership experience and make a meaningful impact.
 Here are some insights to help you get started. Share this with anyone who might find it inspiring!
 
 Meet the current District Team (consult each Team page here) in the District Leadership Handbook:
 
 Leadership roles at the District level
 District Core Team: District Director | Program Quality Director | Club Growth Director (the Trio) Public Relations Manager | Administration Manager | Finance Manager
 District Officers: Division Directors, Area Directors

 Toastmasters learn leadership all along their path, depending on their willingness to take responsibilities within the organization.
